publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: The empiricist distinction between analytic and synthetic truths and the doctrine of reductionism.
span.quote: Modern empiricism has been conditioned in large part by two dogmas.

span.label: Can the analytic/synthetic distinction and reductionism withstand scrutiny, and what follows for empiricism if they cannot?
span.quote: Both dogmas, I shall argue, are ill founded.

span.label: Attacks the two dogmas - the analytic/synthetic distinction and reductionism - arguing for confirmation holism, reshaping twentieth-century analytic philosophy.
span.quote: The unit of empirical significance is the whole of science.

span.label: critique
span.quote: Both dogmas, I shall argue, are ill founded.

span.label: the analytic-synthetic distinction
span.quote: One is a belief in some fundamental cleavage between truths which are analytic , or grounded in meanings independently of matters of fact and truths which are synthetic , or grounded in fact.

span.label: conceptual-analysis
span.quote: Recognizing then that the notation of definition does not hold the key to synonymy and analyticity, let us look further into synonymy and say no more of definition.

span.label: Each proposed explanation of analyticity is shown to presuppose a notion that is itself no clearer than analyticity, so the explanations travel in a circle rather than terminating
span.quote: Our argument is not flatly circular, but something like it. It has the form, figuratively speaking, of a closed curve in space.

span.label: Definition cannot ground synonymy because the lexicographer only records a synonymy that usage already established
span.quote: Certainly the "definition" which is the lexicographer's report of an observed synonymy cannot be taken as the ground of the synonymy.

span.label: Interchangeability salva veritate is too weak in an extensional language and question-begging in a language rich enough to contain 'necessarily'
span.quote: In an extensional language, therefore, interchangeability salva veritate is no assurance of cognitive synonymy of the desired type.

span.label: Appeal to semantical rules fails because 'semantical rule' is itself undefined except by where the phrase is printed
span.quote: Semantical rules are distinguishable, apparently, only by the fact of appearing on a page under the heading 'Semantical Rules'; and this heading is itself then meaningless.

span.label: Because statements meet experience only collectively, any statement can be preserved by revising others, so no statement is analytic in the sense of being immune
span.quote: Any statement can be held true come what may, if we make drastic enough adjustments elsewhere in the system.

span.label: The two dogmas support each other: only if confirmation attaches to statements one at a time does a vacuously confirmed statement make sense
span.quote: as long as it is taken to be significant in general to speak of the confirmation and infirmation of a statement, it seems significant to speak also of a limiting kind of statement which is vacuously confirmed, ipso facto , come what may; and such a statement is analytic.

span.label: the notion of analyticity resists a clear boundary; borderline cases remain undecidable
span.quote: I do not know whether the statement 'Everything green is extended' is analytic.

span.label: Technical problems of ambiguity and homonymy for the proposed formulation of cognitive synonymy are set aside rather than solved.
span.quote: Certain technical questions arise, indeed, over cases of ambiguity or homonymy; let us not pause for them, however, for we are already digressing.

span.label: Not every explanation of analyticity available in the literature is explicitly addressed.
span.quote: Not all the explanations of analyticity known to Carnap and his readers have been covered explicitly in the above considerations, but the extension to other forms is not hard to see.

span.label: The key notion of cognitive synonymy is left uncharacterised within the paper itself.
span.quote: Just what this is cannot be said without successfully finishing the present study; but we know something about it from the need which arose for it in connection with analyticity in Section 1 .

span.label: The paper argues no boundary has been drawn, not that one provably cannot be - the case is the repeated failure of every proposed criterion
span.quote: But, for all its a priori reasonableness, a boundary between analytic and synthetic statement simply has not been drawn.

span.label: Germaneness of a statement to particular experiences is left as a loose association rather than a defined relation
span.quote: But in this relation of "germaneness" I envisage nothing more than a loose association reflecting the relative likelihood, in practice, of our choosing one statement rather than another for revision in the event of recalcitrant experience.

span.label: The positive account of what does guide theory revision is left at the level of conservatism and simplicity, not a criterion
span.quote: Conservatism figures in such choices, and so does the quest for simplicity.

span.label: The author's own inability to classify a sample statement is offered as evidence about the term rather than about his grasp of it, which is asserted rather than shown
span.quote: The trouble is not with 'green' or 'extended,' but with 'analytic.'

span.label: using the physics image of a field of force (with boundary conditions) to model the holistic web of scientific knowledge and its contact with experience
span.quote: total science is like a field of force whose boundary conditions are experience

span.label: cognitive synonymy
span.quote: A natural suggestion, deserving close examination, is that the synonymy of two linguistic forms consists simply in their interchangeability in all contexts without change of truth value; interchangeability, in Leibniz's phrase, salva veritate .

span.label: interchangeability salva veritate
span.quote: A natural suggestion, deserving close examination, is that the synonymy of two linguistic forms consists simply in their interchangeability in all contexts without change of truth value; interchangeability, in Leibniz's phrase, salva veritate .

span.label: physical objects
span.quote: But in point of epistemological footing the physical objects and the gods differ only in degree and not in kind.

span.label: the gods
span.quote: But in point of epistemological footing the physical objects and the gods differ only in degree and not in kind.

span.label: analytic → synthetic
span.note: THE BOUNDARY BETWEEN THESE TWO IS NOT DRAWABLE - the NEGATION of `distinct-from`, and no type we have can express it. All eight types assert that a relation HOLDS; not one can say a relation FAILS, so a paper whose contribution is that a distinction cannot be drawn has no home, and the nearest available move records the distinction as holding. That is exactly what the retracted quine1951[14] did: the paper's DENIAL of the boundary quoted as evidence FOR the boundary. SECOND ATTESTATION, in another field and with no shared vocabulary: Kumar2016 concedes in an fMRI methods paragraph that 'the regressors for the maintenance and encoding phases may be correlated' and 'the activity observed in the maintenance phase may thus be contaminated' - the authors warning they may not reliably tell the two apart, recorded in our corpus as `encoding --distinct-from--> maintenance`. Strip the subject matter and the two papers assert the same relation: THESE TWO CANNOT RELIABLY BE TOLD APART, one argued in philosophy in 1951 and one conceded in a methods note. Neither cites the other and they share no words. Kumar2016 is fenced and is cited here, not touched. Two attestations START A COUNT, they do not license a ninth type.
span.quote: But, for all its a priori reasonableness, a boundary between analytic and synthetic statement simply has not been drawn.

span.label: analytic → synthetic
span.note: THE BOUNDARY BETWEEN THESE TWO IS NOT DRAWABLE - the NEGATION of `distinct-from`, and no type we have can express it. All eight types assert that a relation HOLDS; not one can say a relation FAILS, so a paper whose contribution is that a distinction CANNOT BE DRAWN has no home, and the nearest available move records the distinction as holding. That is exactly what the retracted quine1951[14] did: the paper's DENIAL of the boundary quoted as evidence FOR the boundary. REPLACES unhoused_relations[0], WHICH WAS RETRACTED FOR A CLAIM I ADDED AND GOT WRONG. That row paired this with Kumar2016 as a cross-field attestation - two papers, no shared vocabulary, both asserting that two things cannot reliably be told apart. THE KUMAR2016 HALF WAS A MISREADING: I quoted 'the regressors ... may be correlated' and 'may thus be contaminated' as a concession, when reading the full span shows those clauses SET UP A CONTROL THE AUTHORS THEN PASS - 'the correlation coefficient ... was very small (0.04)'. Kumar2016 asserts SEPARABILITY, with a number. The Quine claim here is unaffected and stands on its own span; only the cross-reference was wrong, and it is not repeated here.
span.quote: But, for all its a priori reasonableness, a boundary between analytic and synthetic statement simply has not been drawn.

span.label: analytic - first class, logical truth: true and staying true under every reinterpretation of everything except the logical particles
span.quote: If we suppose a prior inventory of logical particles, comprising 'no,' 'un-' 'if,' 'then,' 'and,' etc., then in general a logical truth is a statement which is true and remains true under all reinterpretations of its components other than the logical particles.

span.label: analytic - second class, synonymy-dependent: reducible to a logical truth only by putting synonyms for synonyms, and this is the class the paper says cannot be explained
span.quote: The characteristic of such a statement is that it can be turned into a logical truth by putting synonyms for synonyms; thus (2) can be turned into (1) by putting 'unmarried man' for its synonym 'bachelor.'

span.label: analytic - Kant's sense: the subject already conceptually contains the predicate, a formulation the paper faults for assuming subject-predicate form
span.quote: Kant conceived of an analytic statement as one that attributes to its subject no more than is already conceptually contained in the subject.

span.label: analytic - Carnap's sense: true under every state-description, which the paper argues reconstructs only logical truth
span.quote: A statement is then explained as analytic when it comes out true under every state-description.

span.label: analytic - Leibniz's sense: true in all possible worlds, i.e. incapable of being false
span.quote: Leibniz spoke of the truths of reason as true in all possible worlds. Picturesqueness aside, this is to say that the truths of reason are those which could not possibly be false.

span.label: analytic - the self-contradiction sense: a statement whose denial is self-contradictory, rejected as no clearer than what it explains
span.quote: In the same vein we hear analytic statements defined as statements whose denials are self-contradictory.

span.label: synonymy - cognitive: the only sense the argument needs, explicitly not identity of psychological association or poetic quality
span.quote: Now let us be clear that we are not concerned here with synonymy in the sense of complete identity in psychological associations or poetic quality; indeed no two expressions are synonymous in such a sense. We are concerned only with what may be called cognitive synonymy .

span.label: definition - lexicographic report: records a synonymy already implicit in usage, so it cannot be the ground of that synonymy
span.quote: Definitions reporting selected instances of synonymy come then as reports upon usage.

span.label: definition - explication: improves on the definiendum instead of reporting a synonymy, yet still rests on prior synonymies
span.quote: In explication the purpose is not merely to paraphrase the definiendum into an outright synonym, but actually to improve upon the definiendum by refining or supplementing its meaning.

span.label: definition - conventional abbreviation: the sole case where synonymy is genuinely created rather than reported
span.quote: Here we have a really transparent case of synonymy created by definition; would that all species of synonymy were as intelligible.

span.label: reductionism - radical: every meaningful statement translatable into a statement about immediate experience
span.quote: The most naive view of the relationship is that it is one of direct report. This is radical reductionism . Every meaningful statement is held to be translatable into a statement (true or false) about immediate experience.

span.label: reductionism - attenuated: the surviving supposition that a statement in isolation can be confirmed at all, which the paper says is the form that still does damage
span.quote: The dogma of reductionism survives in the supposition that each statement, taken in isolation from its fellows, can admit of confirmation or infirmation at all.

span.label: meaning - as against reference: what essence becomes once it is detached from the object and attached to the word
span.quote: Meaning is what essence becomes when it is divorced from the object of reference and wedded to the word.

span.label: economy - two antagonistic kinds in a formal system: brevity of expression versus poverty of primitive grammar and vocabulary
span.quote: In logical and mathematical systems either of two mutually antagonistic types of economy may be striven for, and each has its peculiar practical utility.

span.label: contradicts → the analytic-synthetic distinction (first dogma of empiricism)
span.quote: That there is such a distinction to be drawn at all is an unempirical dogma of empiricists, a metaphysical article of faith.

span.label: contradicts → reductionism / the verification theory of meaning (second dogma)
span.quote: our statements about the external world face the tribunal of sense experience not individually but only as a corporate body

span.label: builds-on → Carnap, Der logische Aufbau der Welt
span.quote: My countersuggestion, issuing essentially from Carnap's doctrine of the physical world in the Aufbau , is that our statements about the external world face the tribunal of sense experience not individually but only as a corporate body.

span.label: contradicts → Carnap, "Empiricism, Semantics, and Ontology" (1950)
span.quote: Carnap has recognized 12a that he is able to preserve a double standard for ontological questions and scientific hypotheses only by assuming an absolute distinction between the analytic and the synthetic; and I need not say again that this is a distinction which I reject.

span.label: extends → the pragmatism of Carnap, Lewis, and others
span.quote: Carnap, Lewis, and others take a pragmatic stand on the question of choosing between language forms, scientific frameworks; but their pragmatism leaves off at the imagined boundary between the analytic and the synthetic.

span.label: critiques → Carnap's explanation of analyticity by state-descriptions and by semantical rules
span.quote: The criterion in terms of state-descriptions is a reconstruction at best of logical truth.

span.label: critiques → Kant's formulation of the analytic statement
span.quote: This formulation has two shortcomings: it limits itself to statements of subject-predicate form, and it appeals to a notion of containment which is left at a metaphorical level.

span.label: critiques → the term-by-term empiricism of Locke and Hume
span.quote: Moreover, the doctrine is unnecessarily and intolerably restrictive in the term-by-term critique which it imposes.

span.label: extends → Carnap's own treatment of the physical world in the Aufbau
span.quote: My countersuggestion, issuing essentially from Carnap's doctrine of the physical world in the Aufbau , is that our statements about the external world face the tribunal of sense experience not individually but only as a corporate body.

span.label: supports → White's essay on the analytic and the synthetic as an untenable dualism
span.quote: White's excellent essay "The Analytic and the Synthetic: An Untenable Dualism," in John Dewey: Philosopher of Science and Freedom (New York, 1950), says much of what needed to be said on the topic; but in the present paper I touch on some further aspects of the problem.

span.label: Evening Star —same-as→ Morning Star
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: Understood not merely as a recurrent evening apparition but as a body, the Evening Star is the planet Venus, and the Morning Star is the same. The two singular terms name the same thing.

span.label: Evening Star —distinct-from→ Morning Star
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: But the meanings must be treated as distinct, since the identity 'Evening Star = Morning Star' is a statement of fact established by astronomical observation.

span.label: 9 —same-as→ the number of the planets
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: The terms '9' and 'the number of the planets' name one and the same abstract entity but presumably must be regarded as unlike in meaning; for astronomical observation was needed, and not mere reflection on meanings, to determine the sameness of the entity in question.

span.label: creature with a heart —distinct-from→ creature with a kidney
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS STATED IN THE SENTENCE, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE EXAMPLE. 'The general terms creature with a heart and creature with a kidney, e.g., are perhaps ALIKE IN EXTENSION BUT UNLIKE IN MEANING.' The two terms are not distinct simpliciter - they are IDENTICAL on one dimension and different on another, and a bare `distinct-from` records only the second half. Note also that `extension` and `intension` differ by one character, which is why these must never be de-duplicated by edit distance. Q-457. · strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: The general terms 'creature with a heart' and 'creature with a kidney,' e.g., are perhaps alike in extension but unlike in meaning.

span.label: intension —same-as→ meaning
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: It is indeed a commonplace in philosophy to oppose intension (or meaning) to extension, or, in a variant vocabulary, connotation to denotation.

span.label: intension —renamed-across-fields→ connotation
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: It is indeed a commonplace in philosophy to oppose intension (or meaning) to extension, or, in a variant vocabulary, connotation to denotation.

span.label: extension —renamed-across-fields→ denotation
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: It is indeed a commonplace in philosophy to oppose intension (or meaning) to extension, or, in a variant vocabulary, connotation to denotation.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · intension —contrasted-with→ extension
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span named only one endpoint. This sentence names both and states the contrast in the field's own words - to OPPOSE intension to extension. — strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: Now paralleling the contrast between the meaning of a singular term and the entity named, we must distinguish equally between the meaning of a general term and its extension.

span.label: essence —renamed-across-fields→ intension
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9
span.quote: The Aristotelian notion of essence was the forerunner, no doubt, of the modern notion of intension or meaning.

span.label: radical reductionism —is-a→ reductionism
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: More reasonably, and without yet exceeding the limits of what I have called radical reductionism, we may take full statements as our significant units

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · logical truth —part-of→ analytic
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span listed analytic statements without naming logical truth. This sentence names both IN APPOSITION - 'the first class of analytic statements, THE LOGICAL TRUTHS' - which states the containment as directly as Quine states anything. — strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: Statements which are analytic by general philosophical acclaim are not, indeed, far to seek. They fall into two classes. Those of the first class, which may be called logically true, are typified by: (1) No unmarried man is married.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · cognitive synonymy —operationalised-as→ interchangeability salva veritate
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span - 'a natural suggestion, deserving close examination, is that the synonymy of two linguistic forms consists simply in their interchangeability' - states the relation but names NEITHER endpoint as the edge writes them. This span names both and states the same operationalisation. — status: A SUGGESTION UNDER EXAMINATION, NOT A DEFINITION THE ESSAY ENDORSES. Quine offers interchangeability salva veritate as a 'natural suggestion, deserving close examination' and the rest of the paper is the examination that finds it wanting. Without this field the corpus reads as if Two Dogmas defined synonymy this way. · strength of the relation: 0.4 — the record marks this weak
span.quote: A natural suggestion, deserving close examination, is that the synonymy of two linguistic forms consists simply in their interchangeability in all contexts without change of truth value; interchangeability, in Leibniz's phrase, salva veritate .

span.label: analyticity —operationalised-as→ state-description
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.4 — the record marks this weak
span.quote: In recent years Carnap has tended to explain analyticity by appeal to what he calls state-descriptions.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · synonymy —operationalised-as→ method of empirical confirmation
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span named only one endpoint. This sentence names both and gives the operationalisation directly. — strength of the relation: 0.5 — the record marks this weak
span.quote: Then what the verification theory says is that statements are synonymous if and only if they are alike in point of method of empirical confirmation or infirmation.

span.label: RETRACTED (THE SPAN IS THE PAPER'S DENIAL OF THE DISTINCTION, QUOTED AS EVIDENCE FOR IT) · analytic —contrasted-with→ synthetic
span.note: RETRACTED: THE SPAN IS THE PAPER'S DENIAL OF THE DISTINCTION, QUOTED AS EVIDENCE FOR IT. The edge says Quine contrasts `analytic` with `synthetic`. Its span reads 'a boundary between analytic and synthetic statement SIMPLY HAS NOT BEEN DRAWN' - which is the paper's THESIS AGAINST the distinction, not a statement of it. And there is no better span: Quine states the cleavage only as a REPORTED BELIEF he then rejects - 'Modern empiricism has been conditioned in large part by two dogmas. One is A BELIEF IN some fundamental cleavage between truths which are analytic ... and truths which are synthetic'. THE PAPER NOWHERE ASSERTS THE CONTRAST IN ITS OWN VOICE, so there is nothing to re-ground onto. Withdrawn, and logged as a SCHEMA GAP: we have no way to record that a paper is ABOUT a distinction it argues cannot be drawn. — strength of the relation: 0.2 — the record marks this weak
span.quote: But, for all its a priori reasonableness, a boundary between analytic and synthetic statement simply has not been drawn.

span.label: reductionism —same-as→ the analytic and the synthetic
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8
span.quote: The two dogmas are, indeed, at root identical.

span.label: bachelor —same-as→ unmarried man
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.6 — the record marks this weak
span.quote: to say that 'bachelor' and 'unmarried man' are cognitively synonymous is to say no more nor less than that the statement: (3) All and only bachelors are unmarried men is analytic.

span.label: RETRACTED (THE FIFTH QUINE DEFECT AND THE SAME ROOT: A LIKENESS READ AS A DIFFERENCE) · physical objects —distinct-from→ the gods of Homer
span.note: RETRACTED: THE FIFTH QUINE DEFECT AND THE SAME ROOT: A LIKENESS READ AS A DIFFERENCE. The edge says physical objects are distinct from the gods of Homer. Its current span says they 'DIFFER ONLY IN DEGREE AND NOT IN KIND' - a difference explicitly limited to degree - and the best alternative span in the paper says physical objects are posits 'COMPARABLE, EPISTEMOLOGICALLY, TO THE GODS OF HOMER'. BOTH AVAILABLE SPANS ASSERT LIKENESS. Quine's argument is that the two are on the same epistemological footing, which is the opposite of what `distinct-from` records, and it is the same fault as [18] ('in analogy to the irrational numbers') and [14] ('a boundary ... has not been drawn'). A paper that argues by ANALOGY and by DENIAL is mis-tagged in one direction by a vocabulary in which every type asserts that a relation holds. — strength of the relation: 0.15 — the record marks this weak
span.quote: But in point of epistemological footing the physical objects and the gods differ only in degree and not in kind.

span.label: RETRACTED (THE SPAN ASSERTS AN ANALOGY, THE EDGE ASSERTS A CONTRAST) · physical objects —contrasted-with→ irrational numbers
span.note: RETRACTED: THE SPAN ASSERTS AN ANALOGY, THE EDGE ASSERTS A CONTRAST. 'I suggest that experience is ANALOGOUS TO the rational numbers and that the physical objects, IN ANALOGY TO the irrational numbers, are posits which serve merely to simplify our treatment of experience.' Quine is saying physical objects are LIKE irrational numbers - both posits admitted for convenience - which is the whole force of the passage. SECOND QUINE DEFECT TONIGHT, and the same root: this paper argues by stating analogies and denying distinctions, and both were read as assertions of difference. — strength of the relation: 0.9
span.quote: Now I suggest that experience is analogous to the rational numbers and that the physical objects, in analogy to the irrational numbers, are posits which serve merely to simplify our treatment of experience.

span.label: RETRACTED (A NEAR-DUPLICATE OF [17] THAT THE FOLD CANNOT SEE) · physical objects —distinct-from→ the gods
span.note: RETRACTED: A NEAR-DUPLICATE OF [17] THAT THE FOLD CANNOT SEE. Same record, same type, same span to the byte - 'in point of epistemological footing the physical objects and the gods differ only in degree and not in kind' - and the only difference is the endpoint name: `the gods` here, `the gods of Homer` at [17]. The fold keys on (from, to, type, evidence), so a looser spelling of one endpoint produces a second edge asserting the identical thing. Keeping [17], which uses the paper's own fuller phrase. NOTE ALSO, and left standing on [17]: the span scopes its own difference - 'ONLY IN DEGREE AND NOT IN KIND' - and `distinct-from` has no slot for that, so the edge reads as a difference in kind, which is what the sentence denies. — strength of the relation: 0.15 — the record marks this weak — RE-GROUNDS quine1951-two-dogmas[17]: the span stated the relation, the endpoint names did not match its words.
span.quote: But in point of epistemological footing the physical objects and the gods differ only in degree and not in kind.

span.label: cognitive synonymy —operationalised-as→ interchangeability salva veritate
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.4 — the record marks this weak — RE-GROUNDS quine1951-two-dogmas[11]: the relation was always stated, the endpoint names were not in the span.
span.quote: And indeed such an independent account of cognitive synonymy is at present up for consideration, namely, interchangeability salva veritate everywhere except within words.

span.label: intension —contrasted-with→ extension
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — RE-GROUNDS quine1951-two-dogmas[7]: the old span named only ONE endpoint.
span.quote: It is indeed a commonplace in philosophy to oppose intension (or meaning) to extension, or, in a variant vocabulary, connotation to denotation.

span.label: synonymy —operationalised-as→ method of empirical confirmation
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.5 — the record marks this weak — RE-GROUNDS quine1951-two-dogmas[13]: the old span named only ONE endpoint.
span.quote: Statement synonymy is said to be likeness of method of empirical confirmation or infirmation.

span.label: logical truth —part-of→ analytic
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — RE-GROUNDS quine1951-two-dogmas[10]: the old span named ONE endpoint.
span.quote: Our problem, however, is analyticity; and here the major difficulty lies not in the first class of analytic statements, the logical truths, but rather in the second class, which depends on the notion of synonymy.

span.label: Quine argues both central dogmas of empiricism — the analytic/synthetic distinction and reductionism — are ill-founded; abandoning them blurs the boundary between metaphysics and natural science and shifts toward pragmatism.
span.quote: Both dogmas, I shall argue, are ill founded. One effect of abandoning them is, as we shall see, a blurring of the supposed boundary between speculative metaphysics and natural science. Another effect is a shift toward pragmatism.

span.label: The supposed analytic/synthetic boundary has never actually been drawn, despite its a priori plausibility.
span.quote: for all its a priori reasonableness, a boundary between analytic and synthetic statement simply has not been drawn

span.label: no criterion offered for analyticity avoids presupposing a notion as obscure as analyticity itself
span.quote: the notion of self-contradictoriness, in the quite broad sense needed for this definition of analyticity, stands in exactly the same need of clarification as does the notion of analyticity itself.

span.label: definition rests on synonymy rather than explaining it
span.quote: For the rest, definition rests on synonymy rather than explaining it.

span.label: interchangeability salva veritate in an extensional language does not establish cognitive synonymy
span.quote: In an extensional language, therefore, interchangeability salva veritate is no assurance of cognitive synonymy of the desired type.

span.label: appeal to semantical rules of an artificial language does not clarify analyticity
span.quote: Semantical rules determining the analytic statements of an artificial language are of interest only in so far as we already understand the notion of analyticity; they are of no help in gaining this understanding.

span.label: the unit of empirical significance is the whole of science, not the individual statement
span.quote: The unit of empirical significance is the whole of science.

span.label: no statement is immune to revision, including the laws of logic
span.quote: Conversely, by the same token, no statement is immune to revision.

span.label: ontological questions differ from scientific ones only in degree
span.quote: Ontological questions, under this view, are on a par with questions of natural science.

span.label: abandoning the dogmas blurs the boundary between metaphysics and natural science and shifts philosophy toward pragmatism
span.quote: One effect of abandoning them is, as we shall see, a blurring of the supposed boundary between speculative metaphysics and natural science. Another effect is a shift toward pragmatism.

span.label: analytic truths
span.quote: truths which are analytic , or grounded in meanings independently of matters of fact

span.label: synthetic truths
span.quote: truths which are synthetic , or grounded in fact

span.label: reductionism
span.quote: the belief that each meaningful statement is equivalent to some logical construct upon terms which refer to immediate experience

span.label: logically true statement
span.quote: Those of the first class, which may be called logically true, are typified by: (1) No unmarried man is married

span.label: logical truth
span.quote: in general a logical truth is a statement which is true and remains true under all reinterpretations of its components other than the logical particles

span.label: extension
span.quote: The class of all entities of which a general term is true is called the extension of the term.

span.label: state-description
span.quote: A state-description is any exhaustive assignment of truth values to the atomic, or noncompound, statements of the language.

span.label: reductionism
span.quote: The other dogma is reductionism : the belief that each meaningful statement is equivalent to some logical construct upon terms which refer to immediate experience.

span.label: verification theory of meaning
span.quote: The verification theory of meaning, which has been conspicuous in the literature from Peirce onward, is that the meaning of a statement is the method of empirically confirming or infirming it.

span.label: radical reductionism
span.quote: Every meaningful statement is held to be translatable into a statement (true or false) about immediate experience.

span.label: explication
span.quote: I have in mind what Carnap calls explication -- an activity to which philosophers are given, and scientists also in their more philosophical moments.

span.label: primitive notation
span.quote: The inclusive language, though redundant in grammar and vocabulary, is economical in message lengths, while the part, called primitive notation , is economical in grammar and vocabulary.

span.label: extensional language
span.quote: Now a language of this type is extensional , in this sense: any two predicates which agree extensionally (i.e., are true of the same objects) are interchangeable salva veritate .

span.label: analytic
span.quote: a statement is analytic when it is true by virtue of meanings and independently of fact
